problem: Repeated France persistence failures were caused by stale-base/ref races and unnecessary branch/update-ref/PR fallback complexity while main was advancing concurrently.
protocol: Before every canonical mutation, fetch the canonical file from main and parse/recalculate counters from that exact blob.
Persist a new immutable audit file on main with Contents API create_file.
Refetch the canonical from main after the audit write because main has advanced.
Apply only the semantic delta for the current decision to that freshly fetched canonical; never replace it with a full file built from an older base.
Write the canonical with Contents API update_file using the freshly fetched blob SHA as optimistic concurrency control.
If SHA conflict occurs, refetch main, reapply the semantic delta, and retry. Do not create a per-batch persistence branch merely for a stale SHA.
After successful write, refetch canonical and audit from main and verify counters, list lengths, total=291, overlaps/aliases policy, pendingDedupe, latestBatch and decision presence.
Use low-level blobs/trees/commits/update-ref or PR only for exceptional repository recovery, not routine France persistence. Never force-update main.
concurrencyRule: One semantic delta at a time. A writer must rebase logically by refetching canonical after every other write to main. The blob SHA is the lock/version token.
prohibitedRoutinePatterns: full canonical replacement from stale branch
continuing to another CPO before rereading the materialized canonical
